+package cli
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"encoding/json"
+	"errors"
+	"fmt"
+	"io"
+	"strings"
+
+	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/auth"
+	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint"
+	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/id"
+	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/gitremote"
+)
+
+// crossRepoReader is the read surface cross-repo explain needs: the two
+// checkpoint reader tiers the renderers consume, plus the two cross-repo-only
+// extras (author and anchoring commit) that normally come from local git.
+// Narrowed to an interface so tests can drive the render paths without a cell.
+type crossRepoReader interface {
+	checkpoint.CheckpointReader
+	checkpoint.SessionReader
+	GetCheckpointAuthor(ctx context.Context, checkpointID id.CheckpointID) (checkpoint.Author, error)
+	checkpointCommit(ctx context.Context, checkpointID id.CheckpointID) ([]associatedCommit, error)
+}
+
+// newCrossRepoReader builds the API-backed reader for owner/repo. Injectable so
+// tests can substitute a fake cell (see explain_repo_test.go).
+var newCrossRepoReader = func(ctx context.Context, insecureHTTP bool, owner, repo string) (crossRepoReader, error) {
+	ownerRepo := owner + "/" + repo
+	// Resolve the repo_id and the cell together, from one placement: a mirror id
+	// is only resolvable by the cell holding that placement, so a
+	// separately-chosen cell (the caller's home cell, for a multi-region repo)
+	// would be asked about an id it has never seen and answer 404.
+	placement, err := resolveRepoCellPlacement(ctx, owner, repo)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("resolve %s: %w", ownerRepo, err)
+	}
+	client, err := auth.NewEntireAPICellClient(ctx, insecureHTTP, placement.Target)
+	if err != nil {
+		// NewEntireAPICellClient already returns user-facing, context-rich
+		// errors (login hint, discovery guidance); surface them verbatim.
+		return nil, err //nolint:wrapcheck // pass through contextual auth errors
+	}
+	return newAPICheckpointReader(client, placement.RepoID, ownerRepo), nil
+}
+
+// crossRepoReadKey marks a context as rendering a checkpoint read from another
+// repo. Context-scoped like gitrepo.WithStatusCache / checkpoint's remote-list
+// discovery, so the renderers can adjust their guidance without an extra
+// positional parameter through every formatCheckpointOutput call site.
+type crossRepoReadKey struct{}
+
+// withCrossRepoRead marks ctx as reading ownerRepo's checkpoint from that
+// repo's cell.
+func withCrossRepoRead(ctx context.Context, ownerRepo string) context.Context {
+	return context.WithValue(ctx, crossRepoReadKey{}, ownerRepo)
+}
+
+// crossRepoReadSource returns the repo a checkpoint is being read from when the
+// current render is a cross-repo one.
+func crossRepoReadSource(ctx context.Context) (string, bool) {
+	ownerRepo, ok := ctx.Value(crossRepoReadKey{}).(string)
+	return ownerRepo, ok && ownerRepo != ""
+}
+
+// crossRepoExplainOptions carries what `explain --repo` needs to render a
+// foreign repo's checkpoint.
+type crossRepoExplainOptions struct {
+	repoFlag string
+	// target is the checkpoint the user asked for, before ID validation.
+	target string
+
+	json          bool
+	transcript    bool
+	rawTranscript bool
+	// sessionIndex is -1 for "latest session".
+	sessionIndex int
+
+	verbose bool
+	full    bool
+	noPager bool
+
+	insecureHTTP bool
+}
+
+// parseExplainRepoFlag parses `--repo`. Accepted shapes are `owner/name` and
+// `gh/owner/name` (leading slash optional), matching the `repo` field of
+// `entire search` results, which is where a cross-repo checkpoint ID comes
+// from. Returns lowercased coordinates, as the control plane persists them.
+//
+// A bare repo ID is deliberately not accepted: the control plane and the search
+// index expose different identifiers for a repository, and guessing which space
+// an opaque ID belongs to would key the cell lookup off the wrong one.
+func parseExplainRepoFlag(value string) (owner, repo string, err error) {
+	v := strings.TrimSpace(value)
+	if v == "" {
+		return "", "", errors.New("--repo requires a value: owner/name or gh/owner/name")
+	}
+	if !strings.Contains(v, "/") {
+		return "", "", fmt.Errorf("invalid --repo %q: expected owner/name or gh/owner/name", value)
+	}
+	// Normalize to the gh/owner/name clone-ref shape so the mirror parser's
+	// GitHub charset validation applies to both accepted forms.
+	ref := strings.TrimPrefix(v, "/")
+	if !strings.HasPrefix(ref, "gh/") {
+		ref = "gh/" + ref
+	}
+	_, owner, repo, err = parseMirrorCloneRef(ref)
+	if err != nil {
+		return "", "", fmt.Errorf("invalid --repo %q: expected owner/name or gh/owner/name: %w", value, err)
+	}
+	return owner, repo, nil
+}
+
+// explainRepoTargetsCurrentRepo reports whether the --repo value names the repo
+// checked out here. An unparseable value returns false so the cross-repo path
+// runs and reports the parse error, rather than silently falling through to the
+// local path.
+func explainRepoTargetsCurrentRepo(ctx context.Context, repoFlag string) bool {
+	owner, repo, err := parseExplainRepoFlag(repoFlag)
+	if err != nil {
+		return false
+	}
+	return explainRepoIsCurrent(ctx, owner, repo)
+}
+
+// explainRepoIsCurrent reports whether owner/repo names the same repository as
+// the cwd worktree's origin remote (which handles ssh, https, and entire://
+// mirror URL forms). --repo is GitHub-scoped, so a non-GitHub origin with a
+// coincidentally matching owner/name must not match. Best-effort: any lookup or
+// parse failure returns false and the cross-repo path runs.
+//
+// When it does match, explain falls through to the local path — which is both
+// faster and strictly more capable, since it can read checkpoints that have not
+// been pushed yet.
+func explainRepoIsCurrent(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string) bool {
+	curForge, curOwner, curRepo, err := gitremote.ResolveRemoteRepo(ctx, "origin")
+	if err != nil || curForge != "gh" {
+		return false
+	}
+	return strings.EqualFold(curOwner, owner) && strings.EqualFold(curRepo, repo)
+}
+
+// runCrossRepoExplain explains a checkpoint owned by another repository by
+// reading it from that repo's cell over HTTP. Nothing is written to the local
+// repository: no ref, no objects, no session state — so a foreign checkpoint
+// never shows up in this repo's own checkpoint history or token profile.
+//
+// The output modes reuse the same renderers as the local path, so a foreign
+// checkpoint prints identically to a local one.
+func runCrossRepoExplain(ctx context.Context, w, errW io.Writer, opts crossRepoExplainOptions) error {
+	owner, repoName, err := parseExplainRepoFlag(opts.repoFlag)
+	if err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	ownerRepo := owner + "/" + repoName
+
+	// A prefix can't be resolved without listing the foreign repo's
+	// checkpoints, which is `entire search`'s job, so cross-repo needs the
+	// whole ID.
+	cid, err := id.NewCheckpointID(opts.target)
+	if err != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("--repo requires a full checkpoint ID (12-char hex or 26-char ULID); a prefix cannot be resolved in another repo: %w", err)
+	}
+
+	reader, err := newCrossRepoReader(ctx, opts.insecureHTTP, owner, repoName)
+	if err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	// Marked for the renderers: a foreign checkpoint cannot be written to, so
+	// they must not offer actions that only work in the owning repo.
+	ctx = withCrossRepoRead(ctx, ownerRepo)
+
+	stop := startSpinner(errW, fmt.Sprintf("Reading checkpoint %s from %s", cid, ownerRepo))
+	// Read directly rather than through checkpoint.ReadCheckpoint: the helper
+	// prefixes "read persistent checkpoint:", which buries the reader's
+	// already-user-facing message (e.g. the not-pushed-yet guidance) behind
+	// storage vocabulary that means nothing for a repo read over HTTP.
+	summary, err := reader.Read(ctx, cid)
+	if err != nil {

333			url.PathEscape(r.repoID), url.PathEscape(checkpointID.String()))

335		if err != nil {
336			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read checkpoint %s from %s: %w", checkpointID, r.ownerRepo, err)
337		}
338		defer resp.Body.Close()
339	
340		if err := api.CheckResponse(resp); err != nil {
341			if api.IsHTTPErrorStatus(err, http.StatusNotFound) {
342				// Lead with the cause that is overwhelmingly the common one. A
343				// checkpoint only becomes visible here once it has been pushed
344				// and ingested, and most local checkpoints in an active repo are
345				// not pushed yet.

350			}

352		}

354		var env apiCheckpointEnvelope
355		if err := api.DecodeJSON(resp, &env); err != nil {
356			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read checkpoint %s from %s: %w", checkpointID, r.ownerRepo, err)
357		}
358		if env.Checkpoint == nil {
359			return nil, fmt.Errorf("checkpoint %s is not available for %s (the server returned no checkpoint)", checkpointID, r.ownerRepo)

361		if len(env.Checkpoint.Sessions) == 0 {
362			return nil, fmt.Errorf("checkpoint %s in %s has no sessions to explain", checkpointID, r.ownerRepo)

365		r.detail = env.Checkpoint
366		r.detailID = checkpointID
367		return r.detail, nil

370	// parseAPITime parses the first parseable RFC3339 timestamp from the given
371	// candidates. Returns the zero time when none parse, which renders as "unknown"
372	// rather than as a wrong date.
373	func parseAPITime(candidates ...string) time.Time {
374		for _, c := range candidates {
375			if c = strings.TrimSpace(c); c != "" {
376				if t, err := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, c); err == nil {
377					return t
378				}
379			}
380		}
381		return time.Time{}
382	}

1	package cli
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"fmt"
6		"strings"
7		"time"
8	
9		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/auth"
10		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/logging"
11		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/coreapi"
12	)
13	
14	// cellResolveTimeout bounds the best-effort control-plane lookups that
15	// pick a repo's cell. Without it, a reachable-but-hung control plane would block
16	// the calling command (experts, and any future cell-routed command) instead of
17	// degrading to home-jurisdiction routing — the "any failure falls back" contract
18	// must hold for slow cores, not just erroring ones.
19	const cellResolveTimeout = 5 * time.Second
20	
21	// requiredCellResolveTimeout bounds the control-plane lookups a repo-scoped
22	// cell read cannot proceed without (resolveRepoCellPlacement).
23	//
24	// Deliberately not cellResolveTimeout: that budget bounds *best-effort* lookups
25	// whose failure silently degrades to home-jurisdiction routing, so it can be
26	// aggressive. Here a timeout is a visible command failure, and the budget has
27	// to cover two sequential control-plane round trips (the repo's mirrors, then
28	// the cluster catalog), so it is more patient.
29	//
30	// Some deadline is required: the coreapi HTTP client sets only a dial timeout,
31	// so a reachable-but-slow core is otherwise unbounded, and this runs before the
32	// command's spinner starts — the user would sit in front of a silent terminal.
33	const requiredCellResolveTimeout = 15 * time.Second
34	
35	// cellCoreClient is the control-plane surface the cell-target resolver needs.
36	// An interface (with a swappable constructor) so the resolver is unit-testable
37	// against a fake control plane; *coreapi.Client satisfies it.
38	type cellCoreClient interface {
39		GetRepo(ctx context.Context, params coreapi.GetRepoParams) (*coreapi.Repo, error)
40		ListClusters(ctx context.Context) (*coreapi.ListClustersOutputBody, error)
41		ListMirrors(ctx context.Context, params coreapi.ListMirrorsParams) (*coreapi.ListMirrorsOutputBody, error)
42	}
43	
44	// newCellCoreClient builds the control-plane client used for cell resolution.
45	// Swapped in tests.
46	var newCellCoreClient = func() (cellCoreClient, error) { return coreapi.New() }
47	
48	// resolveRepoCellTarget resolves the entire-api cell that HOSTS the given
49	// repo, plus that cell's jurisdiction, so a repo-scoped call (experts today)
50	// reaches the region that owns the repo — mirroring how the entire.io BFF
51	// selects a cell per repo (resolve-cluster-host.ts / repos-stream.ts) rather
52	// than using the caller's home cell.
53	//
54	// It is deliberately best-effort: ANY failure (not logged in, control-plane
55	// error or timeout, unknown/ambiguous placement, missing apiUrl) returns nil,
56	// and the auth-layer client falls back to home-jurisdiction routing. That
57	// fallback is exactly the previous behaviour, so this can never regress the
58	// common same-region case (where the repo's jurisdiction equals the caller's
59	// home). A short deadline keeps a slow control plane from stalling the command.
60	//
61	// Placement source:
62	//   - ulid form: coreapi.GetRepo(ulid) -> Repo.ClusterHost;
63	//   - owner/repo form: coreapi mirrors filtered to this repo -> ClusterHost.
64	//
65	// The cluster host is then mapped to a cell apiUrl + jurisdiction via the
66	// coreapi cluster catalog (ListClusters), the authoritative source for a
67	// jurisdiction's cell URL.
68	func resolveRepoCellTarget(ctx context.Context, fullName, ulid string) *auth.CellTarget {
69		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, cellResolveTimeout)
70		defer cancel()
71	
72		c, err := newCellCoreClient()
73		if err != nil {
74			logging.Debug(ctx, "cell target: core client unavailable, using home-jurisdiction routing", "error", err.Error())
75			return nil
76		}
77	
78		clusterHost, ok := resolveRepoClusterHost(ctx, c, fullName, ulid)
79		if !ok || clusterHost == "" {
80			return nil
81		}
82	
83		return cellTargetForClusterHost(ctx, c, clusterHost)
84	}
85	
86	// cellTargetForClusterHost maps a known cluster host to a cell apiUrl +
87	// jurisdiction via the coreapi cluster catalog, the authoritative source for a
88	// jurisdiction's cell URL. Returns nil for every unresolvable case so callers
89	// fall back to home-jurisdiction routing.
90	func cellTargetForClusterHost(ctx context.Context, c cellCoreClient, clusterHost string) *auth.CellTarget {
91		clusters, err := c.ListClusters(ctx)
92		if err != nil {
93			logging.Debug(ctx, "cell target: list clusters failed, using home-jurisdiction routing", "error", err.Error())
94			return nil
95		}
96		cluster, ok := matchClusterByHost(clusters.Clusters, clusterHost)
97		if !ok {
98			logging.Debug(ctx, "cell target: no cluster matched repo host, using home-jurisdiction routing", "cluster_host", clusterHost)
99			return nil
100		}
101		apiURL := strings.TrimRight(strings.TrimSpace(cluster.ApiUrl.Or("")), "/")
102		// DNS is case-insensitive; normalise the catalog jurisdiction so a
103		// non-lowercase value still passes the auth layer's strict label check
104		// instead of hard-failing the target path.
105		jurisdiction := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(cluster.Jurisdiction))
106		if apiURL == "" || jurisdiction == "" {
107			logging.Debug(ctx, "cell target: matched cluster missing apiUrl/jurisdiction, using home-jurisdiction routing", "cluster_host", clusterHost)
108			return nil
109		}
110		return &auth.CellTarget{BaseURL: apiURL, Jurisdiction: jurisdiction}
111	}
112	
113	// repoCellPlacement is one active mirror placement: the id entire-api keys
114	// repo-scoped routes on, paired with the cell that actually holds it.
115	type repoCellPlacement struct {
116		// RepoID is the mirror id, which entire-api uses as its repo_id.
117		RepoID string
118		// Target is the cell hosting THIS placement.
119		Target *auth.CellTarget
120	}
121	
122	// resolveRepoCellPlacement resolves a GitHub repo to one active placement's
123	// (repo_id, cell) pair for repo-scoped cell reads.
124	//
125	// The pair must come from the same placement: each placement has its own mirror
126	// id, and only the cell hosting that placement can resolve it. Taking the id
127	// from one placement and routing to a cell chosen some other way — the caller's
128	// home cell, say — asks a cell about an id it has never seen, which comes back
129	// as an indistinguishable 404. That is also why this does not reuse
130	// resolveRepoCellTarget's owner/repo path: that one deliberately refuses to pick
131	// among multi-region placements and falls back to the home cell, which is
132	// exactly the mismatch to avoid here.
133	func resolveRepoCellPlacement(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string) (repoCellPlacement, error) {
134		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, requiredCellResolveTimeout)
135		defer cancel()
136	
137		c, err := newCellCoreClient()
138		if err != nil {
139			return repoCellPlacement{}, fmt.Errorf("control plane unavailable: %w", err)
140		}
141		mirrors, err := listMirrorsForRepo(ctx, c, mirrorCloneProviderGitHub, strings.ToLower(owner), strings.ToLower(repo))
142		if err != nil {
143			return repoCellPlacement{}, cellPlacementError(ctx, owner, repo, fmt.Errorf("list mirrors for %s/%s: %w", owner, repo, err))
144		}
145		for i := range mirrors {
146			if !isActiveMirror(mirrors[i]) {
147				continue
148			}
149			repoID := strings.TrimSpace(mirrors[i].MirrorId)
150			clusterHost := strings.TrimSpace(mirrors[i].ClusterHost)
151			if repoID == "" || clusterHost == "" {
152				continue
153			}
154			target := cellTargetForClusterHost(ctx, c, clusterHost)
155			if target == nil {
156				// The catalog can't place this cluster; try the next placement
157				// rather than falling back to a cell that doesn't know this id.
158				continue
159			}
160			return repoCellPlacement{RepoID: repoID, Target: target}, nil
161		}
162		// A deadline that fired mid-loop leaves cellTargetForClusterHost returning
163		// nil for every placement, which would otherwise be reported as "no
164		// reachable mirror" — a wrong diagnosis for a slow control plane.
165		return repoCellPlacement{}, cellPlacementError(ctx, owner, repo,
166			fmt.Errorf("no reachable Entire mirror for %s/%s", owner, repo))
167	}
168	
169	// cellPlacementError reports a timeout as a timeout. The underlying lookups
170	// degrade quietly (cellTargetForClusterHost logs and returns nil), so without
171	// this a fired deadline surfaces as whichever "not found" message the caller
172	// reached, and the user goes looking for a missing mirror instead of a slow
173	// control plane.
174	func cellPlacementError(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string, fallback error) error {
175		if ctxErr := ctx.Err(); ctxErr != nil {
176			return fmt.Errorf("resolving the Entire mirror for %s/%s timed out: %w", owner, repo, ctxErr)
177		}
178		return fallback
179	}
